Declare a step or inverse decay for an FCA specification

Source: R/01-decay_objects.R
decay_step.Rd

Experimental. decay_step() and decay_inverse() are decays for the specifications of floating catchment area indices (spec_2sfca(), spec_e2sfca() and the others). They are neither estimated nor available to an allocation model such as spec_clm(), which refuses them.

Usage

decay_step(threshold)

decay_inverse()

# S3 method for class 'spax_fca_decay'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spax_fca_decay'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

threshold

A single finite number greater than 0: the largest travel time in the catchment.

x

A decay object.

...

Unused.

Value

A spax_fca_decay: a list with method ("binary" and sigma, the threshold as a double, or "inverse" with no sigma).

Details

decay_step(threshold) gives weight 1 to a travel time up to threshold and weight 0 beyond it (the catchment of the two-step method). decay_inverse() gives the weight 1 / (d + 1) to a travel time d, as the "inverse" method of calc_decay() does. They are stored as list(method = "binary", sigma = threshold) and list(method = "inverse"), the form the FCA functions take in decay_params.

See also

Other access interface: spec_2sfca()

Examples

decay_step(15)
#> <spax decay> step (threshold): 15
decay_inverse()
#> <spax decay> inverse: 1/(d + 1)
